text: Right, so if you also see how i said something about a ~45tick/min system, this ties directly into that LoS comment i just said with compute. npc activity only has to progress a state in the immediate LoS so effectively the world around the player stays still. this lets us setup something like this npc has a very specific behavior like fighting other npcs but none of that needs to occur until the player is directly in LoS of that other NPC.
resolution: Adopted the user's stronger simulation ruling (no code): the unseen world is FROZEN, not slowly simulated — offline NPCs are thin state rows with no behavior/perception/pathing executing; the 45/min state-tick and the event channel are the only movers of frozen state. The user's fighting-NPC example formalized as LATENT dispositions: 'this NPC fights that NPC' is editor-authored entity data that only materializes as running behavior when the activation gate reaches it, hydrating mid-action so the world never reads as booting. Named the shipped precedent (STALKER A-Life online/offline split) and the compute consequence: simulation cost is O(active bubble), constant in city size. Recorded in memory project_map_format.md.
